classification.difficultyReason: Source MASTERY, NAPLAN B+: infer the exposed lengths of overlapping rectangle halves and add the exterior sides.

content.prompt: Pablo cuts a paper rectangle in half. He then places one half over the other to make a new shape. What is the perimeter of the new shape?

spec.description: A 16 cm by 3 cm rectangle, midpoint dashed cut line, dimension lines with end marks, and scissors below the cut.
spec.mathematics: The midpoint cut produces two 8 cm by 3 cm rectangle halves.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions and the cutting cue are visible.

spec.description: Upright L-shaped union with overall height and width both labelled 8 cm, and a vertical internal seam below the inside corner.
spec.mathematics: Two 8 cm by 3 cm rectangles overlap in a 3 cm by 3 cm region; the two exposed inner edges each measure 5 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied overall dimensions are visible; inferred lengths and perimeter remain in answer content.

answer.worked:
Each rectangle half is $8\text{ cm}$ long and $3\text{ cm}$ wide. Each exposed inner side is $8-3=5\text{ cm}$. Add only the outside edges.
$$\begin{align*}P&=3+5+5+3+8+8\\P&=32\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
